newsitem.title: USA: Flextronics targets FY97 income growth.
newsitem.headline: Flextronics targets FY97 income growth.

text.p: Flextronics International Ltd Senior Vice President Dennis Stradford said the company is targeted to produce net income of $23.4 million and earnings per share of $1.62 for the 1997 fiscal year.
Stradford noted the analyst projection in a presentation at a Montgomery Securities investment conference here.

Montgomery analysts project Flextronics net sales for the fiscal year to March 31 will grow to $560 million,up from $448.4 million in fiscal 1996. The company sells sophisticated electronics and low-cost manufacturing capacity for customers in the medical, information systems and consumer markets.
Prior to a $31.6 million acquisition-related write off and one-time charges of $2.5 million, it posted net income of $16.6 million and earnings per share of $1.25 in fiscal 1996.

Stradford and Flextronics Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Marks said the company is part of a $56 billion industry growing to $100 billion over the next few years, with outsourcing of electronic assembly within the industry expected to grow over the next several years.
The company's top five customers now account for 43 percent of its business, down from 61 percent when the company completed an initial public offering in March 1994, they said.
They also said the company has roughly halved labor costs to 4.4 percent of sales in 1995 from 8.5 percent in 1990.

Having also cut factory cycle time from five days in 1993 to 40 minutes currently, the executives said the company has embarked on a major effort to lower costs of logistics, and has also targeted miniaturization as a key market expertise.
